newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber up on short covering, tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber up on short covering, tight supplies.

text.p: Thai rubber prices were boosted on short-covering and tight supplies of RSS3 grade rubber over the past few days, traders said on Wednesday.

Thai government's shift of delivery date from June and July to May forced some shippers to seek RSS3 in the market to cover obligations, resulting in tighter supplies, they said. "But many shippers object to the idea and I heard discussion is ongoing to change the delivery date," a Bangkok-based trader said.
"Some shippers do not have much stock and they are not willing to buy at current prices to cover the contracts either," said a Bangkok-based trader.
Rubber prices rose partly on the back of news that the government has approved a decision to raise its support price for rubber to 29.00 baht ($1.15) a kg from 27.50 baht.

But at the same time, the government, which bought around 45,000 tonnes of RSS3 in the FOB market since early March, said it would try to avoid further buying directly in the physical FOB market to prop up prices. It also asked that their purchases be delivered by end-May.
"This move is intended to force traders and shippers to buy in teh domestic market and consequently support the prices," said a Hat Yai trader.
Japan entered the market to buy RSS3 this week while buying from China was still absent, trader said.
"The purchase from Japanese buyers were not big but they had to bid high because of the tight supplies of RSS3," added the Hat Yai trader.
The benchmark RSS3 was indicated at 114.0 U.S. cents a kg for August shipment and 112.50 cents a kg for July shipment. Last week, July shipment was quoted at 109.00 cents a kg.
